evidence: grep -rn 0o666 pycore/pyctl/agent_history: empty. PROMPT_ARCHIVE_FILE_MODE is gone, and no new mode literal was added. prompt_archive.py:40/:123 use root_spool.SPOOL_FILE_MODE, and agent_history_txt.py:30 imports SPOOL_DIR_MODE and SPOOL_FILE_MODE from root_spool.py:44-45.

prompt_archive.py:101-107,121: chmod runs only when the appended batch holds a root-only entry. Nothing ever widens a file, and a file that never receives such an entry gets no chmod. The skip is the condition os.name != "nt", not an except. The failure path logs ColorPrint.yellow with path, oct(mode) and errno (:124-128).

agent_history_txt.py:45-54 _restrict_mode, :57-63 _restricted_dir, :66-74 store_dir/sessions_dir and :93-94 _atomic_write: the store dirs get 0750 and every store file gets 0640, with the same nt condition and logging. The member restricts the whole store unconditionally because index.txt/prompts.txt/state.txt mix root-only and ordinary sessions. The item text says the store is created with the same restricted modes, so this reading is accepted.

Import graph: agent_history_txt -> root_spool adds no cycle. root_spool's top-level imports are only pyfoundations.agent_home_scanner and system_paths. Its root-side function imports (extractor_registry and the extractors) never reach agent_history_txt, store_dir or prompt_archive (grep of the *_extractor.py files, extractor_registry.py and ai_sources.py is empty). The root_spool process therefore never creates or chmods the store.

Refuted in part: the report says the nt condition and logging go 'via a shared _restrict_mode helper'. That helper is private to agent_history_txt.py, and prompt_archive.py:121-128 re-implements the same logic inline (see issues[0]).

issues: B2 duplicate implementation (AGENTS.md: 'reuse or upgrade existing components', 'remove duplicate implementations'; PYTHON_PYCORE.md section 1 and the code-leader audit rule 'shared libraries over copies'): pycore/pyctl/agent_history/prompt_archive.py:121-128 copies the helper this same change adds at pycore/pyctl/agent_history/agent_history_txt.py:45-54 (the os.name == 'nt' condition, then os.chmod in try, then ColorPrint.yellow with path/oct(mode)/errno). prompt_archive.py:39 already imports from agent_history_txt. Fix: make the helper public as one shared function, e.g. restrict_mode(path, mode, label) in agent_history_txt.py (or next to SPOOL_DIR_MODE/SPOOL_FILE_MODE in root_spool.py; pick one place and record the choice). Call it from both modules. In prompt_archive.py, replace :121-128 with 'if has_root_only: restrict_mode(path, root_spool.SPOOL_FILE_MODE, <label>)' and drop the imports that become unused ('import os' at :33 and the ColorPrint import at :41). Keep the log fields unchanged. Keep each file's line endings: prompt_archive.py is LF and agent_history_txt.py is CRLF. Verify with py_compile and grep. Then either rerun the member's WSL Debian temp-dir scratch run (0640 for a root-only sample, the default mode for a non-root sample, never widened, store 0750/0640) and the native Windows no-error run, or, if the resource guard blocks it, record that the change is a pure extraction.
non_blocking: Optional, to fold into the helper when it is made public: every call to store_dir() and sessions_dir() now does mkdir plus chmod, and that includes read paths (snapshot_cache.py:70/:92, agent_history_statistics.py:297, agent_history_fragments.py:102). If the store dir belongs to another uid (for example, a pycore run as root created it first), every call logs a yellow line. pycore/pyutils/common/user_data_store.py:146-152 (_tighten_mode) already has a guard for this: it chmods only when st_uid == os.geteuid() and the permission bits differ. Reuse that guard in the shared helper. The per-call chmod itself is useful: it re-tightens the store after the recursive chmod noted under cross_scope.

Optional: agent_history_txt.py:84-94 _atomic_write chmods only after os.replace. The replaced file briefly has the umask default, and it stays at that mode if the chmod fails. pycore/pyfoundations/atomic_json_store.py:41-45 chmods the temp file before the replace. Follow that order. Exposure is already contained by the 0750 store dir.

prompt_archive.py:101,107: has_root_only is computed only over fresh (non-duplicate) entries. Pre-fix archive files that the old code created as 0o666 and that already hold spooled prompts are tightened only when a new root-only prompt for that tool arrives. The 0750 store dir contains this, so it is acceptable as is.

No chown is applied. This is correct: the non-root worker cannot chown to root and must keep append access to its own files. The item text 'root:<worker gid> 0640' describes the root-spool side. Record this decision in the report in the next round.
prompt_archive.py:118-120: the inline comment repeats the new module docstring paragraph at :21-26. AGENTS.md says 'code is documentation', so drop one of them when the file is next edited.
